questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'. To whom did you give the packet?
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'.

To whom did you give the packet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. No error

Key Points

  • As we know that "who" is used for the subject of the verb, "whom" is used for the object
  • In the case of Passive voice-  it swaps the subject and object; thus, the usage of the preposition 'to' is correct because 'whom ' is the object of 'give to'
    • For e.g.- Whom I talked to. [Here, 'I' is the subject and 'whom' is the object of 'talked to']
  • Also, the subject of the sentence is 'you', the helping verb is 'did', the main verb is 'give', the object of the sentence is 'the packet' and the preposition 'to', the preposition always has a prepositional object, so 'whom' is the prepositional object which is written in the starting of the sentence.
  • Hence, the given sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Notwithstanding we were / all busy that weekend / we had to / cancel the outing.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Notwithstanding we were / all busy that weekend / we had to / cancel the outing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Notwithstanding we were'.
Key Points
  •  In the given sentence, the main focus is on the reason to cancel the outing.
  • Reason can be expressed with the words like because or as.
    • As we were all busy that weekend we had to cancel the outing.
  • The use of notwithstanding is inappropriate here.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 3.
Additional Information
  • Notwithstanding (preposition) means 'despite the face or thing mentioned.'
    • Notwithstanding severe headache, he gave the presentation.
    • Many criticisms notwithstanding, this movie broke the record.

Key Points
  • The error in the sentence is in the segment 'discusses is funny, playing'. The error lies in the usage of 'playing'. 
  • The adjectives 'funny', 'playing' and 'mischievous' are used to describe the art.

questions.question: Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall looking for packets of ready to cook food.

options.html: packets of ready to cook food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'in the mall looking for'

Key Points

 In the given sentence, the usage of 'in the mall looking for' is incorrect Instead, use 'in the mall were looking for'

  • According to grammar, 'Most of' is a quantifier which is used to 'to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.'
  • In the given sentence, 'that clause' is used which has its own subject which is 'shoppers' hence we need a verb for this subject because it is not mentioned in the sentence. 
  • So we need a plural verb which should be in the past tense because the main clause of the sentence is in the past tense.
  • So use 'were looking'

So the correct sentence is- We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall were looking for packets of ready to cook food.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. There is a whole world / out there that / is invisible from / the naked eye.

The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: is invisible from

Key Points

  • The error here lies in the choice of the correct preposition.
  • Replace "from" with "to" in order to correct the sentence.
  • From is used to refer to the place where someone or something starts or originates.
  • To is used to indicate the person or thing that receives or experiences the object of the verb.
  • Here, the action is "invisible" and the receiver is "the naked eye."
  • So, the preposition "to" should be used here.
  • Thus, the correct answer is option 2, which contains an error in it.

 

Corrected sentence: There is a whole world out there that is invisible to the naked eye.

questions.question: Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Here, in truth, lies / the crux of the / great problem of all.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Here, in truth, lies / the crux of the / great problem of all.
questions.solution: The phrase "great problem of all" should be "great problem of everything." Superlative adjectives are used to compare three or more things and indicate the highest degree of a quality. When using superlatives with "the," we typically use "the" before the superlative adjective to specify that it is the highest or lowest degree of a particular quality within a certain group. Structure: With definite article "the" + superlative adjective. Correct sentence: Here, in truth, lies the crux of the greatest problem of all.

questions.question: Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Our twenty-first-century society expects all relevant information to simply be handing to us.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Our twenty-first-century society expects all relevant information to simply be handing to us.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "handing to us".

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the form of the verb 'handing' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is in the passive voice as in the passive voice, there are only the verb and the object, no subject to be mentioned.
  • We form the passive with be + past participle (third form of the verb).
  • Therefore, the present participle form 'handing' should be replaced by the past participle form 'handed'.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: Our twenty-first-century society expects all relevant information to simply be handed to us.

He was formerly / a doctor of / the corporate hospital.
questions.solution: In the given sentence, the usage of the preposition 'of' is incorrect. We use the preposition 'of' usually to talk about quantification, the relation of an object with a noun, and for reference. We use the preposition 'at' to talk about time, location or activity. In the given sentence, we need to use the preposition 'at' as we are giving details about the place where the doctor was working. The correct sentence is: He was formerly a doctor at the corporate hospital.

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: in India known

Key Points

  • Replace "known" with "know" to correct the sentence.
  • “Know” is the present tense form of the verb “to know”.
  • “Known” is the past participle of the verb “to Know”. 
  • The given sentence is written in the simple present tense and in the question form.
  • So, we have to use the present form of the verb that is "know"

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which contains an error.

Corrected sentence: How many languages do most children in India know?

questions.question: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. We were busy at the work and went for lunch only at 2.30 pm.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

We were busy at the work and went for lunch only at 2.30 pm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is at the work​​.

Key Points​

  • ​There are some fixed prepositional phrases given below:
    • ​by the dint of, at work/home, come in contact with something, by the dozen, owing to, on a trip, for a change, etc.
  • For example:
    • If he’s not at home, he must still be at work.
  • ​The phrase 'at work' means at the place where one works​. In this phrase, A/an is not used.
  • Thus the 2nd option is the correct choice.
     

Correct Sentence: We were busy at work and went for lunch only at 2.30 pm.

Additional Information

  • There are some verbs/nouns/adjectives which are followed by fixed preposition given below:
    • ​Exonerate from, refrain from, suspicious of, interested in, inured to, accused of, a predilection for, a respite from, vexed at, etc.
  • Example:
    • ​After spending some time on the island they became inured to the hardships.
